title: Huge relief rally: S&P +4.7%, Nvidia +31.5%
detail: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after US authorities said he posed no security threat; the stock jumped 31.5%, Micron 19%, Intel 16%. The S&P 500 rose 4.7% and the Nasdaq 6.5%, the biggest gains since April 2025; the VIX fell 26% to 26.6. The S&P is still ~7% below its October high.
implication: Removes the main idiosyncratic shock, but one-day rebounds after corrections are common; credit and the Fed remain the tests.

title: Credit strain: SpaceX $32bn bond clears only at steep yields
detail: SpaceX's $32bn debt sale only cleared at steep yields during the sell-off. Gold had its worst week in ~8 months as investors sold to raise cash. Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed against tightening too aggressively.
implication: The first sign the equity rout is reaching financing markets; AI-linked and high-yield borrowers are most exposed.

title: Fed still ~93% priced to hike on 9 Dec
detail: Despite the sell-off, markets price ~93% odds of a 25bp hike; Waller floated 50bp and Daly said more hikes may be needed. October PCE (+0.3% m/m expected) and the Q3 GDP revision are due this week.
countries: US TR ZA BR AR IN ID
implication: Hiking into a market rout raises recession risk; a softer Fed would ease EM currencies and the dollar.

title: US-Iran: talks signal vs. Gulf attacks; Hormuz flows fall
detail: JD Vance reportedly discussed possible talks with Tehran with Qatar's prime minister, pushing Brent below $89, a 3-month low. But the IRGC fired missiles and drones at US positions in Bahrain, the Houthis claim a hit on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery, and Kpler says Hormuz flows fell to ~9.5 mb/d in the 10 days to 19 Nov from 12.2 mb/d in October. Iran wants the blockade lifted before fully reopening the Strait.
countries: SA JP KR IN CN TR IT EA
implication: Oil is pricing a deal and a glut; falling Hormuz flows and attacks on Gulf refineries are the risk that is not priced. Importers (JP, KR, IN, TR, IT) are most exposed.

title: France contraction deepens; Germany booms
detail: November flash composite PMI: France 46.2 (48.1 expected), the steepest contraction since May, with manufacturing down to 47.9; Germany 55.0, its strongest since March 2022. Euro-area composite steady at 51.7. Australia's flash composite fell to 46.1, the weakest since Aug 2021.
implication: A widening core split: French assets and the OAT-Bund spread carry the risk, while German cyclicals hold up. In Australia, it adds to the case that the RBA over-tightened.

title: Bank of Korea expected to hike to 3.25%
detail: The BoK decides on 26 Nov and is widely expected to hike 25bp despite the KOSPI at a 10-month low.
implication: Another central bank tightening into a sell-off; the won and Korean chip stocks are the pressure points.

title: Australian unemployment jumps to 4.9%
detail: The highest since Oct 2021; employment fell 43,500. The ASX has fallen eight sessions in a row. October CPI is due this week.
implication: Raises the risk the RBA over-tightened; AUD, banks and housing-linked stocks carry the downside.

title: South Africa: inflation 5.2%; SARB split
detail: October CPI rose to 5.2% from 4.5%; SARB held at 7.25% with three of seven members voting to hike.
implication: A January hike is live; rand and local bonds are exposed.

title: Bank Indonesia surprises with a hike to 6%
detail: BI raised rates 25bp with inflation only 3.23% to defend the rupiah.
implication: Strong-dollar pressure is forcing EM central banks to tighten; watch IN, TR and ZA.

title: China October data miss
detail: Industrial production +4.8% y/y vs 5.3% expected; retail sales +0.4% vs 0.8%. Beijing has since rolled out measures to support the stock market.
implication: Weak China demand weighs on commodity exporters (AU, BR) and Korean suppliers.

title: Japan Q3 GDP flat; Tokyo CPI due
detail: Q3 GDP 0.0% q/q; October CPI 2.3%. Tokyo November core CPI is expected at 3.0% this week, raising December BoJ hike odds. Nikkei fell 5% on 20 Nov.
implication: A BoJ hike with the yen near 159 could trigger carry-trade unwinds.

title: Euro-area inflation 4.0%; Italy 5.5%
detail: Final October HICP confirmed at 4.0%; Italy's national CPI rose to 5.5%. Flash November CPI for France and Spain due this week.
implication: ECB hike bias persists while growth slows; periphery spreads widen first.

title: UK and Canada retail sales beat
detail: UK October +2.3% y/y vs 1.7% expected; Canada September +7.5%. UK consumer confidence improved to −22.

title: Baltic Dry steady near 2,900
detail: −2.8% on the week; still +8% on the month.

title: Spain snap election on 29 Nov
detail: A domestic political event; limited global spillover unless it unsettles periphery spreads.
